channel.title: Murtaza Bagwala — Blog
channel.description: Software Craftsman. Exploring the world of AI and Machine Learning. Always learning.

item.title: How I Fine-Tuned TinyLlama on My Laptop Using LoRA
item.description: A complete walkthrough of fine-tuning a 1.1B parameter model on a Mac using LoRA, merging the adapter, and serving it locally with Ollama.

item.title: Building the Harness: How Real ML Systems Actually Run Models
item.description: You trained the model. Now what? This post explains model inference and harness engineering with real code and zero hand-waving.

item.title: Cognitive Offloading vs Cognitive Surrender: One Makes Sense, the Other Doesn't
item.description: Cognitive offloading is smart. Cognitive surrender is dangerous. A Wharton study of 1,372 people shows most of us have stopped telling the difference.

item.title: The Person Who Writes the Best Skills Wins
item.description: Skills are becoming the new language for AI tools. Write a better skill and the LLM doesn't just follow instructions, it starts thinking like you.

item.title: AI Tells You What to Build. Engineers Know Why It's Complicated.
item.description: AI can generate a product plan in minutes. That doesn't mean it can be shipped in the same time. Here's the part the hype doesn't talk about.

item.title: How I used Logistic Regression to Calculate Compatibility Scores in a Dating App
item.description: How can a simple statistical model make digital interactions feel personal? In a dating app project I worked on, I used logistic regression to turn user answers into meaningful insights. This blog shares my approach and the lessons I learned along the way.

item.title: Asking Questions: The Most Underrated Skill
item.description: From everyday life to professional growth, asking the right questions can unlock understanding, insight, and opportunity.

item.title: How I use AI tools like Cursor and Warp in my daily workflow
item.description: Practical examples of how I use Cursor (AI editor) and Warp (AI terminal) to refactor code, write tests, and speed up everyday tasks with prompts, examples, and images.

item.title: Rails adds include_seconds option to datetime_field.
item.description: Rails now allows to omit seconds part in the input field by adding the include_seconds option to datetime_field.

item.title: Rails preserves entry TTL when incrementing or decrementing an integer value.
item.description: Rails now preserve expires_in while incrementing or decrementing an integer value in MemoryStore to be more consistent with MemCacheStore and RedisCacheStore.

item.title: How to set up a CI/CD workflow for Expo React Native application using Github Actions.
item.description: In this blog, we will see how to set up a CI/CD workflow using Github Actions for the Expo React Native application.

item.title: Rails adds beginless range support to clusivity
item.description: Rails now adds support to include the beginless range in active record inclusivity/exclusivity validators.

item.title: Rails avoids queries when performing calculations on contradictory relation
item.description: Rails now avoids making a query to the database if the calculation contains a contradictory relation.

item.title: Overuse of Rails engines
item.description: In this post, we will see how the overuse of engines could lead to some serious issues.

item.title: Rails for Multi database defines reading_request? in resolver
item.description: Rails moves reading_request? method from the DatabaseSelector to the DatabaseSelector::Resolver class so that we can override the method in custom Resolver.

item.title: Rails allows specifying the maximum number of records that will be destroyed in a single background job.
item.description: Rails adds an active record configuration to limit the maximum number of dependent records destroyed in a single background job.

item.title: Rails allows using aliased attributes with insert_all and upsert_all
item.description: Rails is continuously adding convenience to make active record queries more flexible. Now, Rails has added support to use aliased attributes with insert/upsert_all.

item.title: Know how to rollout and rollback deployments in Kubernetes
item.description: As people and businesses increasingly depend on SaaS products, DevOps have started on creating reliable infrastructure. Reducing deployment downtime is at the top of their priority list. In this post, we will see how Kubernetes handles this gracefully.

item.title: Ruby 3.1 introduces Variable Width Allocation for Strings
item.description: In this blog let us understand how Variable Width Allocation works in Ruby

item.title: How does Ruby manage memory?
item.description: Each programming language has its version of memory management so, let us look into how Ruby does this under the hood.
